title: System One for claims
text: I built Claims One as an independent concept for TypeSafe AI and Jev. This is a mock reference, not live inference.

title: One state. Six questions.
text: I submit a synthetic dental claim. One batch evaluates six independent questions, then ordinary code composes the route.

title: The published primitive contract
text: Choice and Score show full probability distributions and confidence. Scores display one to five, with the raw zero-based value explained. Noul returns only its value.

title: Same answers. Different delegation.
text: At eighty-five percent, this claim needs human review. I lower the threshold to sixty-five: simulated auto-approve. The answers stay unchanged. Safety holds cannot be overridden.

title: Published assumptions, explicit units
text: Fifty thousand claims at fifteen hundred input tokens each illustrate three dollars fifteen monthly. The comparator comes from published ratios, not independent pricing or measured performance.

title: Synthetic evaluation, visible denominators
text: The shared threshold updates this two-hundred-and-forty-row synthetic evaluation. Counts and denominators expose the tradeoff; these are not measured Jev accuracy.

title: The thinking ships, too.
text: Finally, my local documentation records the product decisions, contract, tests, and limitations. This is a reference to inspect, not a live insurance service.
